thesis: Responsibility is a justifiable relationship, not a single property inferred from outcomes.

ideas.statement: Causal, retrospective, role, prospective, reparative and legal responsibility differ.
Moral luck and causal determination complicate desert without erasing meaningful differences between coercion and deliberation.
Social existence does not establish moral legitimacy; obligations must be justified to those burdened.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: An engineer can owe new inspections without being guilty of a collapse.
A public acceptance of responsibility matters only through explanation and correction.
The bridge example separates causal contribution, blame and duties to prevent further harm, resisting scapegoats and total exemption.
Reliable performance can serve injustice, while accountability requires practical consequences rather than a public formula.
Unequal circumstances and opportunities qualify moral comparison; ignorance and deliberate avoidance need different assessments.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Ultimate moral ontology remains disputed; not all ignorance is culpable.

audit.notes: All assigned units read. Claims remain bounded; hypothetical cases are not empirical evidence.
